description: Linux CI drill proving a sealed Preview spool survives the original manager lifetime and can be bind-mounted into a fresh Docker container that reopens the spool and executes ResumeCommit using only PostgreSQL. The producer remains the host test process, so this is a durable-remount foundation and not a producer-container or host restart proof.
requiredAssertions: source fetch and parser seal complete before the forced PostgreSQL commit outage
failed commit leaves zero durable Preview rows
sealed spool exists after the failed commit
the original spool manager is closed before the recovery container starts
a fresh Docker container bind-mounts the same spool directory
the recovery container constructs Flow with Spool and Committer only
ResumeCommit succeeds without object-store or parser access
the first successful recovery is not mislabeled as a replay
the exact same spool ID is independently verified after remount
exactly one Preview with two candidates and one rejection is committed
implementationGuards: Docker execution is explicitly gated and skipped in ordinary unit/race suites
the helper test binary is built with CGO disabled for container portability
PostgreSQL is reached through host.docker.internal host-gateway mapping
database URLs are sanitized from any persisted diagnostic output
request and spool mounts contain only synthetic test data
raw database URL and MinIO credentials are never written to result evidence
limitations: producer remains the host Go test process
producer host or container is not terminated and restarted
fresh container performs only spool reopen, independent verification and ResumeCommit
ephemeral PostgreSQL 16 and MinIO dependencies only
not a reviewed production parser artifact
